body:
You are drafting spoken lines for a video game. Reply with plain text only, in the exact row format given at the end of this message. Do not send messages to anyone else and do not ask questions: decide. Write nothing but the rows (no title, no notes, no Markdown).

THE GAME. "The Crooked Moon" is a single-player, turn-based tactical party RPG built from a folk-horror Dungeons and Dragons campaign. It is set in Wickermoor Hollow, a haunted valley in Druskenvald, a land of endless night under a giant Crooked Moon with a crone's face. The look is a Halloween that never ends, drawn like an 1980s cartoon. A ghost train, the Ghostlight Express, has crashed in the valley; the party is stranded in the Hollow and its village, Wickermoor. The tone is warm, wry and funny on the surface, with real dread and real grief underneath. The player controls a party of four chosen from six companions: Rook Coldwake, Tobin Hayward, Silas Vane, Delphine Ravelle, Lucan Houndstooth and Cordelia Skein. They are quirky, capable adults.

THE NARRATOR. A NARRATOR row is spoken by the Vagrant, the green-skinned ferryman of the ghost train, who tells the tale in a folksy Southern drawl. At the camp fire he is warm and wry, and when a talk turns sad his humour leaves and he goes plain and level. He speaks to the party as "you" and about the companion in the third person, by first name. Present tense, one or two sentences, under about 32 words. Concrete senses (a smell, a sound, a touch, what the hands are doing) over adjectives. Never tell the player what to feel. Never "suddenly". No facts the party could not see. Drop the final g ("hangin'") in about one Narrator row in four, and use no other dialect spelling. He is kind, never mocks a stumble and never makes light of the dead.

RULES FOR EVERY LINE.
1. The companion's voice sheet below comes first. Match its accent, pace, vocabulary and contractions, and the existing lines. Use a pet phrase at most twice in the whole reply and never twice in one talk. Never repeat or closely paraphrase a line already in the voice sheet or the note.
2. A SAY row is the companion speaking: one or two short sentences, under about 28 words. Never put three sentences in one row; start another row instead.
3. The party's options (OPTION rows) are under 12 words, in the plain voice of the party, work at any hour and in any weather, never name a hero, and are never rolls or checks. A reply must always answer the option it follows.
4. Canon limits. Use only the facts in the voice sheet and the note below. Do not invent a new named person, place, monster, event, object the companion carries, or piece of the companion's history. You may invent small, harmless habits, fondnesses, superstitions and turns of phrase, and the look of the fire and the night. Name no place that the note does not name. Never state a dark secret. You may come close to one and step back.
5. Nothing here is a game system: no dice, no checks, no points, no levels, no HP, no "approval", no menus talked about aloud. Plain punctuation only (commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, question marks, quotation marks inside a line when someone is quoted). No em dashes, no semicolons, no brackets, no asterisks, no stage directions, no placeholders.
6. Humour comes from the character, never explained. The sad turn is plain and short.
7. Our own words. Nothing quoted from any book.

THIS REQUEST. Region banter for The Crooked Nightmare: 8 short exchanges between two or three companions, spoken as the party walks about this place. There are no Narrator rows, no options and no replies. Every row is a companion talking to another companion, never to the player.

HOW IT WORKS. When the party comes into an area, now and then one exchange plays as a few lines of chat between companions who happen to be in the party, once each. Only two or three of the six are ever in the party, so each exchange stands alone, mentions nobody else and needs no setup. Each one below is about what is in front of the party in one place at one moment of the story. Banter is funny first; one line in an exchange may turn honest, never more. The chat is about the place: what it looks and smells like, what is odd or sad or silly in it, and how each companion's trade, habits and fears meet it.

RULES.
1. Each exchange is 4 to 6 SAY rows, each a companion's single line (one or two short sentences, under about 28 words), alternating naturally between the speakers; every speaker listed speaks at least once.
2. Use only the facts in the attached cast sheets and the "In front of them" facts of that exchange. The "Story now" line is everything the party knows of the story: a remark must never run ahead of it (name a villain, a fight or a result only if the Story now line does). Never state or hint at any companion's past or secret, and never say what anyone's debt is. No new named people, places or monsters.
3. Pet words and phrases: each companion's at most once in an exchange, and never in two consecutive lines. Companions call each other by first name.
4. No two exchanges may share a joke or a topic, and no line may repeat a line in a cast sheet. Spread the topics: do not make every exchange about the same kind of thing.
5. Plain punctuation only (commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, question marks, quotation marks). No em dashes, semicolons, brackets, asterisks or stage directions. No game terms. Our own words.
AVOID in this region: What Rook hears in the ruins and what Cordelia meets at the crater are their own scenes: nobody hears a voice or names a meteorite's meaning. Everything here is a dream: nobody explains it. Do not describe the Crooked Man.

THE EXCHANGES (in this order):
EXCHANGE 1: Rook + Delphine (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, delphine_ravelle)
  Story now: The party stands before the cleansed manor, which has bent crooked again.
  In front of them: The Druskenvald Estate, crooked again: The cleansed manor bent crooked again: walls weeping purple slime, red lights flaring in the windows and going dark, screams from inside. The hill road climbs to the iron gate, and the house waits beyond it, every line of it bent. Purple slime runs down the clapboard, a window flashes red, then black. On the porch a small girl and a red dog are quarrelling over the ... Parts of it: The gate; The wrap-around porch; The pond; The kitchen gardens; The barns' yard; The hill road; The dead tree. Things to see: The manor's front door; The open gate; The pond; The big barn; The small barn; The dead tree; A well; A signpost at the gate; A broken signpost. People here: Dani; Shuck.
EXCHANGE 2: Tobin + Silas (speaker ids: tobin_hayward, silas_vane)
  Story now: The party is in an autumn wood under a full moon, with handprints on the trees.
  In front of them: The Dark Wood: An autumn wood under a full moon, handprints on the trees, a clearing with a small girl in it. An autumn wood of beech, ash and hickory, blue and grey in a full moon with no face on it. White handprints, small and bright, mark the trunks every few strides, and ahead the trees open on a clearing. Parts of it: The wood; The moonlit clearing. Things to see: The handprint trail begins; A tree with a white handprint; A beech in the dark; Leaf litter; A crooked door in the leaves, covered in handprints; A stump with a bite out of it. People here: Little Adela.
EXCHANGE 3: Delphine + Lucan (speaker ids: delphine_ravelle, lucan_houndstooth)
  Story now: The party has come to a moonless meadow wedding feast. Lucan's hound may be called Barnaby now and is known to fear thunder.
  In front of them: The Wedding Feast: A moonless meadow wedding: long tables, a ring of masked dancers, a dais with a bride and a goat. A moonless spring night, and a meadow in flower. Lanterns hang on poles. Two long tables groan with food, a ring of guests in animal masks turns in a dance, and on a raised dais a bride in a crown of roses stands beside a black go... Parts of it: The meadow; The dais; The dance ring. Things to see: The wedding, from the lane; The dance ring; A long table of food; The gory feast table; The dais; Flower crowns on a pole; A wedding lantern; A guest in an animal mask, still as a post. People here: Bride Adela; Tamsin Ledger.
EXCHANGE 4: Tobin + Cordelia (speaker ids: tobin_hayward, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The party has come to a room-sized brick oven, blazing.
  In front of them: The Oven: A room-sized brick oven, blazing: a roast on one spit, a captive on the other. The kitchen oven of the Crooked House, grown to the size of a room: firebrick, iron spits, and a heat that presses on the eyes. A turkey-reptile roasts on one spit, and a woman hangs chained on the other. Parts of it: The oven. Things to see: The heat of the oven; The fire, behind the bricks; An iron spit as long as a barn; A turkey-reptile on a spit, roasting; A locked chain; A crank the size of a wheel; A rack of pots; A crooked door, in the flames. People here: Gilly Jenkin; Stonoga, in the dream.
EXCHANGE 5: Rook + Lucan (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, lucan_houndstooth)
  Story now: The party has been shrunk and stands on a shelf in the library. Lucan's hound may be called Barnaby now and is known to fear thunder.
  In front of them: The Shelf: The party, shrunk, on a shelf in the library: book spines for walls, a decanter the size of a tower, a cat's face at the open edge. You are the size of a thimble, on a shelf in the library, and every book is a wall. A decanter stands over you tall as a tower with a man in it up to his waist in rising liquor. Beyond the plank's open edge a cat's face the size o... Parts of it: The shelf. Things to see: The shelf; A decanter the size of a tower; A wall of book spines; A book, lying on its back like a hill; Dust, like snow. People here: Walter Jenkin; Golub, in the dream; Wisp, in the dream.
EXCHANGE 6: Tobin + Delphine (speaker ids: tobin_hayward, delphine_ravelle)
  Story now: The party has come to the swollen attic with its seething walls and clawed cauldron.
  In front of them: Toil and Trouble: The attic swollen with old rituals, its walls one seething layer of vermin, a clawed cauldron over a fire. The attic of the Crooked House, swollen and fouled by every ritual it has ever seen. Its walls are a single seething layer of weasels, centipedes and pigeons. On a floor scrawled with sigils a huge clawed cauldron boils over a fir... Parts of it: The attic. Things to see: The attic, from the stair; A clawed cauldron, boiling; A seven-pointed star in the floor; Bones, gnawed; A wrecked trunk; Cobwebs and feathers; Scrawled sigils; A swollen crib; A wrecked rocking chair. People here: Stonoga, in the dream; Golub, in the dream; Vessla, in the dream.
EXCHANGE 7: Tobin + Lucan (speaker ids: tobin_hayward, lucan_houndstooth)
  Story now: The party stands in a smoking crater under a clean half-moon. Lucan's hound may be called Barnaby now and is known to fear thunder.
  In front of them: The Smoking Crater: A crater under a clean half-moon, a prismatic meteorite in it, a city's lights across the bay. A cool summer night and a clean half-moon. Across a little bay stand the lights of a great modern city. In front of you the earth is scorched in rays round a smoking crater, and in it a seven-foot stone pulses in every colour ther... Parts of it: The crater's rim; The crater. Things to see: The crater's rim; The meteorite, pulsing; The lights of a great city, across the bay; Scorched earth; A stone; A bench from another world. People here: Teenage Adela.
EXCHANGE 8: Silas + Delphine (speaker ids: silas_vane, delphine_ravelle)
  Story now: The Crooked House has fallen. The party is among the ruins under a clear sky.
  In front of them: The Druskenvald Estate, in ruins: A heap of wood, plaster and dust under a clear sky, where the Crooked House stood; spirits swirling round it like wasps round a broken hive. The manor is gone. Where it stood lies a heap of broken timber and plaster, and over it, under a clean starry sky, the freed spirits turn and turn. A small girl stands calm in the middle of it. Parts of it: The gate; The wrap-around porch; The pond; The kitchen gardens; The barns' yard; The hill road; The dead tree. Things to see: The open gate; The pond; The big barn; The small barn; The dead tree; A well; A signpost at the gate; A broken signpost; The porch steps. People here: Dani; Shuck.

THE ROW FORMAT (exact). One row per line:

EXCHANGE <number>
SAY <speaker id>: <line>
SAY <speaker id>: <line>
...

Use the speaker ids exactly as given (for example SAY rook_coldwake: ...). Write exactly 8 EXCHANGE blocks, numbered 1 to 8, and nothing else.

ATTACHED DOCUMENTS. Two documents come attached to this message; read both before you write: `tasks/crooked-moon-companions/banter-cast-1.md` (the voice sheets and fact lists for Rook Coldwake, Tobin Hayward and Silas Vane) and `tasks/crooked-moon-companions/banter-cast-2.md` (the same for Delphine Ravelle, Lucan Houndstooth and Cordelia Skein).

EXCHANGE 1
SAY rook_coldwake: We signed that house off as level, Delphine, and now the gables are forty degrees out of regulation and weeping purple muck onto the porch. Settle down now, I am writing a second citation.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Save your chalk, darling, when a house bends on the bias and flashes red for the cheap seats, it is staging a revival, not asking for a mason.
SAY rook_coldwake: A revival still needs proper drainage round the well, and my brass knocker has not stopped clacking since we passed the broken signpost.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Your Foolishness just tried to rhyme clapboard with encore, Rook, which is frankly more offensive than the screaming behind that door.
SAY rook_coldwake: Put a thumb in my ribs if I forget to breathe before the porch steps. I hate clearing the same docket twice.

EXCHANGE 2
SAY tobin_hayward: Beech, ash and hickory, Silas, and the leaf litter tastes of chalk and cold knuckles. Someone has been slapping white handprints up the bark like a lunatic marking rows for felling.
SAY silas_vane: Tell's in the twitch, friend, and those little prints are dealing straight toward that crooked door in the leaves. Somebody stacked this wood for a very small player.
SAY tobin_hayward: Look at the bite taken out of that stump, clean through the heartwood. Whatever chewed it did not care for the grain.
SAY silas_vane: My shadow is lagging a full stride back under this blank moon, Tobin, and it does not rattle unless the house is palming a nasty card.
SAY tobin_hayward: Keep your bone cards in your fist and walk by the turnip light, then. We will see what is waiting in the clearing before the damp gets in my stitches.

EXCHANGE 3
SAY delphine_ravelle: Now that is proper billing, Lucan, animal masks in the dance ring and a black goat sharing the dais with the bride. In Picco we charged two silver extra for livestock in the ceremony.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: The choreography is lively, Delphine, though the gentleman in the mask by the pole has not shifted his posture in ten minutes. I can only award the catering a three, as half the long table is raw offal.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Mind the seams, darling, if that goat starts taking vows, I am stealing the rose crown for my lining.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Barnaby is tucking his tail behind my boots, if you please, and there is not a cloud of thunder in this moonless sky.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Keep your hand on his collar and your yellow eyes on the lanterns, Lucan. Nobody sets a feast this big unless they expect the guests to stay on the platter.

EXCHANGE 4
SAY cordelia_skein: Fascinating pathology, Tobin, the thermal ratio inside this firebrick chamber could render a specimen down to tallow in twelve minutes flat. Do look at the size of that iron wheel.
SAY tobin_hayward: Keep three paces between me and the grate, Cordelia, I am dry straw from collar to heel and the draught is already curling my cuffs. Even the mice in my lapels have gone still.
SAY cordelia_skein: Do hold still, darling, I can spin a thin silk screen across your burlap if the heat presses too hard on your eyes.
SAY tobin_hayward: Save your thread for the woman chained to that top spit, before the crank turns her over the coals alongside that ugly roasting bird.
SAY cordelia_skein: My vials are beginning to simmer against my thorax, Tobin, and if my humours boil over, neither of us will remember how to work a lock.

EXCHANGE 5
SAY rook_coldwake: This plank has no proper parapet, Lucan, and the dust is lying two inches thick like Syndramas snow. One bad step off the edge and that cat takes us off the shift log.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Hush now, the dark has teeth, and at our present scale those teeth are the size of churchwarden spades. I must grade the feline an eight for vigilance, though its nose needs wiping.
SAY rook_coldwake: Never mind the cat, there is a fellow up to his waist in a liquor decanter the height of a watchtower, and zero drainage on the glass.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: The bouquet coming off that stopper is three-quarters cheap brandy and one-quarter pure terror, Rook, and Barnaby is barking at the book spines like a terrier at a wall.
SAY rook_coldwake: Keep the little hound off the spilled spirits and mind the turf along the bindings. My fingers are soft enough without climbing wet leather.

EXCHANGE 6
SAY tobin_hayward: Hold still, you're fraying on the stair nail, Delphine, and I will not have centipedes nesting in your hem before we reach the rafters. That whole wall is one living pelt of vermin.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Do not fuss over my stitches, Tobin, look at the state of the house, feathers in the cobwebs and a clawed pot boiling in a seven-pointed star. Whoever dressed this attic had a very loud third act.
SAY tobin_hayward: They had fifty years of sour ritual soaked into the floorboards, more like, and my head is itching with beetles just looking at those gnawed bones.
SAY delphine_ravelle: He says the rocking chair is waiting for an encore, darling, and he is not even making a pun about the crib.
SAY tobin_hayward: Stay three paces back from the cauldron fire and step round the chalk sigils, girl. Some rot you do not scrape with a boot.

EXCHANGE 7
SAY tobin_hayward: I just put a pinch of this crater ash on my tongue, Lucan, and it has no earth in it at all. It tastes like cold iron and colours a turnip never grew under.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Prime specimen of a pit, Tobin, though the spoor around the rim is burnt completely flat. Look across the bay at those thousands of little lamps, all stacked up without a single chimney smoking.
SAY tobin_hayward: Good soil, bad seed, I used to say, yet this seven-foot stone fell straight out of the sky and scorched the taproots into glass.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Barnaby will not go near that strange bench, if you please, and the hair along my own neck is rising at the hum of that pulsing rock.
SAY tobin_hayward: Keep your nose out of the furrow, then, and let us see to the girl on the rim before the light gets into our seams.

EXCHANGE 8
SAY silas_vane: House always wins, unless you burn the house, Delphine, and this one folded all the way down to the cellar. Look at those spirits spinning out of the plaster like sparks off a wheel.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Curtain down, darlings, and not a single rafter left to hang a velvet drape from. Even Your Foolishness has gone quiet over my shoulder, and he usually loves a collapsing set.
SAY silas_vane: That is a clean sky above the dead tree, friend, real stars and no old crone squinting down at my tally marks. Makes a fellow's ribs feel light.
SAY delphine_ravelle: There is not even a brass button in the dust worth pocketing, Silas, just broken timber and a little girl standing by the porch steps.
SAY silas_vane: Leave the trinkets in the dirt and pocket your needle, doll. When the table clears this clean, you take your winnings and walk out the open gate.
